title: Part.Anchored
summary: Whether physics simulation moves the part. Anchored=true: frozen in place (buildings, floors). Anchored=false: simulated — falls, rolls, gets pushed. Most 'why did my part fall' bugs are this.

properties.name: Anchored
properties.description: true = excluded from physics simulation; position stays where set. false = simulated (gravity, forces, collisions).

explanation.whyItExists: Worlds need both immovable architecture and physical objects; one boolean separates them.
whenToUse: Architecture, terrain accents, spawn pads → Anchored
Temporarily anchoring for placement, then unanchoring (build systems)
whenNotToUse: Anchoring things you want to move with physics — tween/CFrame them deliberately instead
tips: A model falls apart at runtime? Some part isn't anchored or welded
AssemblyRootPart determines who 'carries' an assembly — anchoring any part pins the whole welded assembly
Unanchored + CanCollide=false parts fall through the world
commonMistakes: Building in Studio, forgetting to anchor, and watching the build collapse on Play
Moving anchored parts with physics forces (nothing happens) — use CFrames
Network ownership confusion: unanchored parts are simulated by the server or an owning client

examples.title: Runtime spawn with correct anchoring
examples.code:
local platform = Instance.new("Part")
platform.Size = Vector3.new(8, 1, 8)
platform.Anchored = true            -- it's architecture
platform.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
platform.Parent = workspace

local crate = Instance.new("Part")
crate.Size = Vector3.new(2, 2, 2)
crate.Anchored = false              -- it's a physics prop
crate.Position = Vector3.new(0, 12, 0)
crate.Parent = workspace            -- falls onto the platform
